new_entities.name: Regular kombucha intake
new_entities.description: Repeated consumption of kombucha beverages over weeks in free-living adults.

new_entities.name: Human metabolic markers
new_entities.description: Human clinical markers such as lipids, insulin resistance, glycaemia, inflammatory markers, and related cardiometabolic risk indicators.

edges.effect_quant: Two recent kombucha clinical programmes in adults with excess weight found within-group improvements in lipids, oxidative stress, and some insulin-resistance markers, but the strongest randomized trial still reported no significant between-group difference across the total marker set after 10 weeks. That leaves the metabolic signal interesting but not yet decisive.
edges.population: adults consuming black-tea or green-tea kombucha for 4 to 10 weeks, usually with overweight or obesity
edges.mechanism: Kombucha delivers tea polyphenols, fermentation-derived organic acids, and microbial metabolites that may modestly influence oxidative stress handling, adipokine signalling, and insulin sensitivity, but the human signal still looks small and context-dependent.
edges.summary: Human kombucha evidence is still in the promising-but-noisy zone. The better recent trials suggest small cardiometabolic improvements in some settings, yet the clearest randomized data still stop short of showing broad between-group superiority across the whole biomarker panel.
edges.caveats: Most human studies are small, short, and concentrated in a few research groups. This edge is about measurable metabolic markers in humans, not marketing claims about detoxification or dramatic weight loss.

evidence.citation: BonifacioDB et al 2026 J Food Sci
evidence.notes: Effect of Green Tea Kombucha Within an Energy-Restricted Diet on Cardiometabolic Risk Markers in Individuals With Excess Body Weight: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
